entities.summary:
The Book of Sirach, also known as Ecclesiasticus, is a Jewish wisdom text composed in the early 2nd century BCE. Written by Ben Sira, it is part of the Catholic and Eastern Orthodox biblical canons. The book is attributed to the Jewish priest and scribe Ben Sira, who lived in Jerusalem during the Hellenistic period. It contains wisdom teachings, proverbs, and commentary on biblical stories, with a focus on the importance of wisdom, justice, and morality.

The book's significance lies in its influence on Jewish thought and its role in shaping the development of Jewish wisdom literature. It is also notable for its portrayal of wisdom as a key virtue in Jewish tradition. In terms of legacy, the Book of Sirach has had a lasting impact on Christian and Islamic thought, with many of its teachings and themes incorporated into the writings of the early Christian church fathers and Islamic mystics. The book's use of apocalyptic imagery and symbolism also reflects the cultural and theological currents of the time.

One of the most striking aspects of the Book of Sirach is its vivid depiction of the human condition, with its emphasis on the importance of living a virtuous life and cultivating wisdom. This is reflected in its famous saying, 'A house divided against itself cannot stand' ('Sirach 7:1'). This wisdom has resonated with readers across cultures and centuries, making the Book of Sirach a timeless classic of Jewish wisdom literature.
